direct_answer: Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) causes pain and stiffness in the shoulders, neck and hips, usually in people over 50. It is often worse in the morning. It is usually treated with steroids, which need careful monitoring. New headache or vision changes need urgent assessment.
author: Louis Maxwell

content:
PMR can come on quickly and make everyday tasks such as dressing or getting out of bed very hard.

This guide explains PMR and its treatment. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Symptoms

  • Pain and stiffness in shoulders, neck and hips.
  • Stiffness worse in the morning.
  • Tiredness, low mood, weight loss.

Treatment

PMR is usually treated with steroid tablets, reduced slowly over time. Do not stop steroids suddenly.

Steroid side effects

Steroids can affect bones, blood sugar, mood and infection risk. Ask about bone protection and monitoring.

Daily life

  • Plan harder tasks for later in the day.
  • Use dressing aids.
  • Keep gently active.

When to get help

  • Get urgent same-day help (NHS 111, your GP or A&E) if you have a new headache, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing or any change in vision, as this can be giant cell arteritis.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is PMR the same as arthritis?

No, but it is a rheumatic condition.

How long does treatment last?

Often one to two years or more.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Polymyalgia rheumatica
  • NHS: Steroid injections
